why: No page describing this line could be found; searches turned up only the Devil's Thumb hike.

Held at unsure on review: the page covers the approach only, and the normal descent comes down the Athabasca Glacier; round 6 held it for the same reason (researcher: The route page has the approach stay off the glacier, climbs a rock-and-ice gully beside the icefall and rappels the line.)

Held at unsure on review: one account, and the route's own text names glacier travel (researcher: Trip accounts describe snowfields and a snow ramp crossed with axes and no roping, with only a remnant glacier off to the side of the col.)
The area page places this winter icefall in a Waterton drainage a short walk from the road, with no glacier involved.
Only a route-list entry was found, with no description of the line or descent.
Stanley north-side routes are reached over the Stanley Glacier toe, but no page describes this east-end line itself.
